subject: general
question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest accrued on an amount of ₹40,000 in 2 years was ₹324. The rate of interest per annum was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **2 years**, the difference (D) between **CI** and **SI** is given by: D = P × (R/100)²

324 = 40,000 × (R/100)²

(R/100)² = 324 ÷ 40,000 = 81 ÷ 10,000

Taking square root on both sides: R/100 = 9 ÷ 100

R = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹40,000

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Difference (D)** = ₹324

**Formula Used:**

Difference (D) = P × (R/100)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/049665086f63c8d5158450088b6b7b380b7237f8d8fe1be35819baea2c292ee3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 324 = 40,000 × (R/100)²

⇒ (R/100)² = 324 ÷ 40,000

⇒ (R/100)² = 81 ÷ 10,000

⇒ R/100 = √(81 ÷ 10,000)

⇒ R/100 = 9 ÷ 100

⇒ R = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Simple Interest (SI)

SI is calculated only on the principal amount: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

CI is interest calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest: CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1].
